<summary>
Turn 31: Opened agentops/__init__.py; saw it imports langchain callback handlers unconditionally and also contains redacted placeholders in the init signature (api_key=***REDACTED***). 

Turn 32–33: Wrote patch_2.diff to wrap langchain_callback_handler imports in a try/except and set handler symbols to None when ImportError occurs. First attempt to apply patch_2.diff failed with “corrupt patch at line 22”.

Turn 34–36: Inspected patch_2.diff and agentops/__init__.py; determined the unified diff hunk header/context was wrong. Rewrote patch_2.diff with corrected hunk ranges and context.

Turn 37: Re-applied patch_2.diff successfully; patch applied cleanly to agentops/__init__.py.

Turn 38: Reinstalled the package in the older venv (.venv_old) and confirmed `import agentops` now works without langchain installed.

Turn 39: Installed pytest-related deps and ran `pytest -q`. Result: 9 tests passed, 1 failed (tests/test_events.py::TestEvents::test_record_timestamp). Failure: event.init_timestamp == event.end_timestamp even after sleep and calling agentops.record(event). Log shows “🖇 AgentOps: Cannot record event - no current session”, implying record() returned early without updating timestamps.

Turn 40–45: Investigated timestamp/session behavior:
- agentops/event.py: Event sets init_timestamp and end_timestamp via default_factory=get_ISO_time (millisecond precision), so they can be identical at instantiation.
- agentops/client.py: Client.record() immediately returns (with warning) if no active session; end_timestamp correction logic occurs only after that check.
- agentops/worker.py: start_session posts to /sessions and requires HTTP 200, else start_session fails and client keeps no session.
- agentops/http_client.py: request/response parsing and retry behavior reviewed.
- agentops/helpers.py: singleton decorator means Client instance persists across calls/tests; get_ISO_time uses milliseconds.
- agentops/config.py: Configuration raises ConfigurationError if no api_key, causing Client.__init__ to return early (no session). Redacted placeholders are present in this file too (e.g., broken environ.get line and api_key assignment), but execution reached tests, so current observed failing test is due to “no current session” preventing record() from updating end_timestamp.

Net state: packaging patches (patch_1 applied earlier) + patch_2 applied; imports fixed for optional langchain; pytest suite now down to one failing timestamp test caused by record() bailing out when session isn’t started/created.</summary>
